title: AgentOps Pawl Verdict v1
description: The machine-checkable, EVIDENCE-BOUND and COMMIT-BOUND fresh-context-by-default (multi-model opt-in) verdict that authorizes a mutate-shared-trunk pawl (merge/push to main). Written by ao pawl after /pawl-review lanes (or /council) supply evidence; read by scripts/reconcile-pr.sh BEFORE it merges. Green CI is necessary but NOT sufficient: a merge requires this artifact to exist, be tied to THIS bead+PR+head_sha, carry ALL refuters CONFIRMED, meet the pawl's per-MODE diversity floor (fresh-context DEFAULT = >=1 refuter whose context_id != author_context_id, model-agnostic; multi-model OPT-IN = >=2 distinct KNOWN-roster families), and carry real reviewer evidence (a transcript/evidence path that exists and is non-empty, or a council_artifact that exists). Fail-closed by construction: absent artifact, wrong bead/PR, stale-or-unknown head_sha, the per-mode diversity floor unmet (no fresh-context refuter, or — in multi-model — fewer than two KNOWN-roster distinct families), any non-CONFIRMED refuter, missing reviewer evidence, or an escalate/hold disposition => the gate refuses the merge. THREAT MODEL: this defends against a SLOPPY agent that skips the real review and self-stamps CONFIRMED — it requires that a review ACTUALLY RAN (evidence) against the CURRENT commit (head_sha) by reviewer(s) meeting the pawl's diversity mode. It is NOT cryptographic provenance: there are no signatures, no peercred, no OS-level writer separation. Cryptographic un-forgeability against a hostile forger is INTENTIONALLY OUT OF SCOPE (single-operator trusted loop; the cut cathedral). The companion free-form council narrative lives at .agents/council/YYYY-MM-DD-pawl-review-*.md; THIS file is the checkable summary the merge path enforces against. Runtime artifact lives at .agents/pawl-verdicts/<bead-id>.json (untracked); this schema and its fixtures are tracked.

bead_id.description: The bead this verdict authorizes. reconcile-pr.sh requires this to equal the bead it is closing.

pr.description: The PR number this verdict was produced against (>=1), or 0 for push-to-main landings without a PR. reconcile-pr.sh requires this to equal the PR it is merging; check-pawl-pre-push.sh requires pr=0 for direct push-to-main.

head_sha.description: REQUIRED: the PR head commit the panel actually reviewed. reconcile-pr.sh fetches the PR's CURRENT head sha (gh pr view <PR> --json headRefOid) and refuses the merge if this != current — a verdict goes STALE the moment a new commit is pushed, so it can never be reused across a re-push. This is the COMMIT-BINDING half of the gate.

disposition.description: Panel-level disposition. CONFIRMED = ALL refuters confirmed, the per-mode diversity floor is met, and the panel authorizes the door. REFUTED = at least one refuter refuted; the gate REJECTED. The default REFUTED path is AUTO-REJECT -> AUTO-REDO: the loop sends the work back to be re-done with the findings and re-gates, with no human — continuous self-correction. ESCALATE / HOLD = a tunable CIRCUIT BREAKER tripped (max-attempts, time budget, cost/quota budget, or oscillation/no-forward-progress); the loop stops auto-redoing and HOLDs for a human. The disposition is ESCALATE/HOLD ONLY on a breaker trip, NOT on plain REFUTED. REBOUND = a prior CONFIRMED review re-bound onto a new commit only after the executable checker revalidates CONFIRMED lineage, patch-id identity, byte-exact content identity, the full panel/evidence battery, and a green full gate. CONFIRMED or validated REBOUND authorizes the merge; bare or invalid REBOUND, REFUTED, ESCALATE, and HOLD fail closed. The merge-authorization semantics are enforced by pawl-verdict.sh check, not by the enum alone.

generated_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp when the panel recorded this verdict.

mode.description: Which diversity requirement the gate enforces for THIS pawl. fresh-context (DEFAULT) = a genuine fresh red-team: require >=1 refuter whose context_id != author_context_id (a separate invocation that did NOT share the author's accumulated context/tunnel-vision). Family is NOT required to differ — same model in a fresh context catches the author's context-accumulation errors, which is the dominant failure. multi-model (OPT-IN, per-pawl, operator-tunable like the circuit-breaker thresholds) = the stronger door: require >=2 distinct, roster-validated CANONICAL families (all CONFIRMED), which ALSO catches a model's systematic blind spots. Opt up only the highest-irreversibility pawls; keep the default cheap. Absent => fresh-context (default). Everything else in the gate (CONFIRMED, head_sha match, evidence present, schema-valid, terminal CI) is mode-INDEPENDENT.

author_context_id.description: REQUIRED: the authoring worker session's context identifier (its invocation/session id). The fresh-context check compares each refuter's context_id against this: a refuter is a genuine fresh red-team only when refuter.context_id != author_context_id. This is what makes 'fresh-context' VERIFIABLE rather than asserted — a refuter that ran in the author's own context (context_id == author_context_id) cannot satisfy the default diversity requirement.

attempt.description: Which re-gate attempt produced this verdict (default 1). A plain REFUTED auto-redoes (no human); the disposition only flips to ESCALATE/HOLD when a circuit breaker trips — e.g. the max-attempts breaker after N (default 3) re-work/re-gate cycles, or the time/cost/oscillation breakers. Never CONFIRMED on a streak of REFUTEDs.

refuters.description: The refuter panel. EVERY refuter must be CONFIRMED, each prompted to refute, each read-only and stake-free. The DIVERSITY requirement is mode-based (see `mode`): in fresh-context (default) at least ONE refuter must carry context_id != author_context_id (a genuine fresh red-team, model-agnostic) — one fresh refuter suffices; in multi-model (opt-in) at least TWO distinct canonical families must appear. minItems is 1 so a single fresh-context refuter is schema-valid; the per-mode floor (>=1 fresh refuter, or >=2 families) is enforced in pawl-verdict.sh `check`.

family.description: The reviewer's model family, recorded as a label from the KNOWN alias roster (the writer stores the raw label as given). Aliases collapse to three CANONICAL families: fable/anthropic -> claude; codex/openai -> gpt; agy/google -> gemini. This enum admits the full alias set; pawl-verdict.sh `check` then lowercases + normalizes each label to its canonical family and rejects anything off-roster, so a fake/unknown label ('totally-real-family', 'x') is refused at check time — the multi-model '>=2 distinct families' floor cannot be gamed with junk strings (roster validation is mode-INDEPENDENT). In the OPT-IN multi-model mode at least two DISTINCT CANONICAL families must appear across the refuters (e.g. claude + codex passes; claude + fable does not — both canonicalize to claude); the DEFAULT fresh-context mode is model-agnostic and does not require distinct families.

reviewer.description: Optional reviewer/session identifier (must differ from the authoring worker session).

context_id.description: REQUIRED: the context/invocation id this refuter ran in. fresh-context mode (the default) requires >=1 refuter whose context_id != the verdict's author_context_id — proving this refuter was a SEPARATE invocation with no shared accumulated context, not the author re-grading itself. The same model in a fresh context still satisfies fresh-context; a refuter whose context_id == author_context_id is NOT a fresh red-team and does not count toward the requirement.

verdict.description: This refuter's verdict. EVERY refuter must be CONFIRMED for the panel to authorize the door.

evidence.description: Path to this refuter's grounding evidence — the real reviewer run output (transcript), the pinned-fixture sweep, or the council narrative anchor. reconcile-pr.sh requires this file to EXIST and be NON-EMPTY (or the verdict's top-level council_artifact to exist). A verdict with no reviewer evidence anywhere is fail-closed: it reflects an assertion, not a review that actually ran. This is the EVIDENCE-BINDING half of the gate.

council_artifact.description: Optional path to the free-form council narrative (.agents/council/YYYY-MM-DD-pre-land-<slug>.md) this summary was distilled from.

degraded.description: Optional. TRUE when this verdict was produced under a DEGRADED review posture: the panel could not run at its configured strength (e.g. a reviewer family was unavailable and it fell back to a reduced-diversity or cold-fallback path) but a real review still ran. Lets downstream consumers (metrics, audits) distinguish a nominal verdict from one produced under a weaker-than-nominal configuration. Absent => nominal (not degraded).

cost.description: Optional verification-economics meter (age-verification-economics-ebec.1), attached when the reviewer runner passed --wall-seconds. tokens_est carries the REAL harness usage parsed from the refuter evidence (the codex exec 'tokens used' total) with estimated=false when available (age-ivoq); otherwise the flagged transcript-bytes/4 estimate with estimated=true. Projected into the provenance ledger edge (duration_s, tokens_est) by ao provenance emit-verdict.

rebound_from_verdict.description: Optional; part of the REBOUND lineage. Path to (or id of) the prior verdict artifact this one was re-bound FROM — the previously-recorded verdict whose real review this REBOUND descends from. Makes the re-bind auditable: the original review that actually ran is locatable from here.

rebound_from_sha.description: Optional; part of the REBOUND lineage. The commit sha the prior verdict (rebound_from_verdict) actually reviewed. With patch_id_proof it establishes that the commit this verdict is now stamped onto is byte-identical to the originally-reviewed one (only sha/date changed, e.g. after a rebase).

patch_id_proof.description: Optional; part of the REBOUND lineage. The git patch-id proving byte-identity between the originally-reviewed commit (rebound_from_sha) and the new commit this REBOUND verdict points at. A matching patch-id is deterministic evidence the diff is unchanged across the re-bind — what licenses reusing the prior review instead of running a fresh one.
